title: Falcons of love
takeaway: People who ride on hardship reach the goal, and love's falcons fly all the way to heaven.
scene: The poet has spent long, painful hours waiting for the one he loves. He thinks about who actually reaches the goal in life and in love.

original: جو یار دی اڈیک وچ سجناں گزاریاں
بڑیاں ای دلخراش سن گھڑیاں اوہ ساریاں
transliteration: Jo yaar di udeek vich sajnaan guzaariyaan
Badiyaan ee dil-kharaash san ghariyaan oh saariyaan
translation: All the hours I spent waiting for my friend,
every one of them tore at my heart.
couplets.story: Every hour he spent waiting for the Beloved hurt. Waiting was painful, minute by minute.

original: منزل اوہناں دے واسطے نیڑے ہو جاوندی
جو اوکڑاں دی کنڈ تے کردے سواریاں
transliteration: Manzil ohnaan de vaaste nere ho jaandi
Jo aukraan di kand te karde savaariyaan
translation: The destination comes close for those
who ride on the back of hardship.
couplets.story: The goal gets closer for people who don't run from hard times. They climb on top of their problems and ride them like a horse.

original: لکھیا گیا اے مڈھ توں ساڈے نصیب وچ
غم دوریاں دا درد دل تے بے قراریاں
transliteration: Likhiya gaya ae mudh ton saade naseeb vich
Gham dooriyaan da, dard-e-dil te beqaraariyaan
translation: It was written in my fate from the very beginning:
the grief of distance, heartache and restlessness.
couplets.story: He feels it was written in his destiny from the start: missing people, heartache and never being able to settle.

original: نقشے نے رنگ روپ دے اکھاں دے ساہمنے
یاداں کدوں سہانیاں دل نے وساریاں
transliteration: Naqshe ne rang roop de akhaan de saahmne
Yaadaan kadon suhaaniyaan dil ne visaariyaan
translation: Pictures of that beauty are still before my eyes;
when has my heart ever forgotten those lovely memories?
couplets.story: He can still picture the Beloved's face clearly. His heart has never forgotten those beautiful memories.

original: اوہ لوک ای ہمیش دی پاندے نیں زندگی
جنہاں فصیل عشق تے جاناں نے واریاں
transliteration: Oh lok ee hamesh di paande nain zindagi
Jinhaan faseel-e-ishq te jaanaan ne vaariyaan
translation: Only those people gain everlasting life
who have given their lives on the walls of love.
couplets.story: The only people who truly live forever are those who gave their lives defending love, like soldiers on a castle wall.

original: اکھاں دی پیاس دل دی اے دھڑکن بلاوندی
ہنجواں نے تیرے واسطے راہواں سنواریاں
transliteration: Akhaan di pyaas, dil di ae dharkan bulaaundi
Hanjhuaan ne tere vaaste raahvaan sanvaariyaan
translation: The thirst of my eyes, the beating of my heart, keep calling you;
my tears have swept and decorated the paths for you.
couplets.story: His eyes are thirsty to see the Beloved, and his heartbeat keeps calling out. His tears have washed the roads clean, getting them ready for the Beloved to walk on.

original: شہباز عشق مستی دی منزل دے واسطے
کھنباں نوں کھول عرش تک مارن اڈاریاں
transliteration: Shahbaaz ishq masti di manzil de vaaste
Khambaan nu khol Arsh tak maaran udaariyaan
translation: The royal falcons of love, heading for the goal of ecstasy,
spread their wings and soar all the way to God's Throne.
couplets.story: Lovers are like royal falcons. Aiming for the joy of love, they spread their wings and fly so high they reach heaven itself.

original: دلبر دا ساتھ کہکشاں تارے تے چاننی
مڑ کے نہ آئیاں دوستو! راتاں اوہ پیاریاں
transliteration: Dilbar da saath, kehkashaan, taare te chaanni
Mur ke na aaiyaan dosto! Raataan oh pyaariyaan
translation: The beloved's company, the Milky Way, the stars and the moonlight:
friends, those lovely nights never came back!
couplets.story: He remembers nights with the Beloved under the stars and the Milky Way, in the moonlight. Those beautiful nights never came again.

original: مینوں تے جاپدا اے اوہو وے گا کرچیاں
پتھر دے نال لائیاں شیشے نے یاریاں
transliteration: Mainu te jaapda ae oho ve ga kirchiyaan
Patthar de naal laaiyaan sheeshe ne yaariyaan
translation: It seems to me it will end up in splinters:
the glass has made friends with a stone.
couplets.story: He worries this will end badly. It's like glass making friends with a rock. Sooner or later the glass will shatter.

original: جہنے سدا دے ساتھ لئی کیتے قرار سن
اوہنے وی اج ڈھو لئے بوہے تے باریاں
transliteration: Jihne sada de saath layi keete qaraar san
Ohne vi ajj dho laye boohe te baariyaan
translation: The one who promised to be with me forever
has today shut the doors and windows too.
couplets.story: The person who promised to stay with him forever has now closed every door and window on him.

original: دیندا اے دکھ دور توں الفت دا او مینار
احمدؔ لہو دے نال جو نیہاں اساریاں
transliteration: Denda ae dikh door ton ulfat da o minaar
Ahmad lahu de naal jo neehaan usaariyaan
translation: That tower of love can be seen from far away,
Ahmad, whose foundations I laid with my own blood.
couplets.story: He ends proudly. His love is like a tall tower you can see from miles away. He built its foundations with his own blood.

deeper:
'The royal falcons of love soar all the way to God's Throne' (Arsh) makes the spiritual direction clear. The goal of this love is God, at the highest point of creation. The falcon (shahbaz) is also Allama Iqbal's favourite symbol of the soul that refuses to stay low.

'Only those who gave their lives on love's walls gain everlasting life' reflects the belief that what is given for God is never lost. 'Riding on the back of hardship' is a Sufi teaching: trials carry you toward God if you ride them instead of running away.
why: The falcon flying up to heaven, and the tower of love built on blood, are big, memorable pictures of what real commitment looks like.
prompt: What hardship could you 'ride' instead of running from it?
